## pelican-server cache chaos corrupt

Flip bytes in a cached object's block

### Synopsis

Flip bytes in the on-disk (encrypted) representation of a block so that
its authentication tag no longer validates. The cache detects this on the next
cold read of the block or during the periodic data scan, which invalidates and
re-fetches the object.

By default the latest cached version is targeted; use --etag or --instance to
select a specific version.

Examples:
  pelican cache chaos corrupt pelican://my-federation/data/file.dat
  pelican cache chaos corrupt /data/file.dat --block 3 --bytes 32
  pelican cache chaos corrupt --instance &lt;hash&gt; --block 0

```
pelican-server cache chaos corrupt <object-url> [flags]
```

### Options

```
      --block uint32   Zero-based block number to corrupt
      --bytes int      Number of bytes to flip (default: the authentication-tag size)
  -h, --help           help for corrupt
```
